newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil may tighten foreign exchange bands - report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil may tighten foreign exchange bands - report.

text.p: The Brazilian government is studying whether to tighten the spread in its two-band foreign exchange rate system to allow it to adjust the value of the real currency more regularly, a newspaper reported Sunday.

The Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper said Finance Ministry officials were considering narrowing the gap between the maximum and minimum value of the real, currently fixed at 1.06 and 0.97 reais per dollar.
"With a smaller gap between the floor and the ceiling, the band could be altered more regularly, giving more predictability to foreign exchange rate policy," Folha wrote.
The government operates a twin-band system whereby the Central Bank often makes daily adjustments to the mini-band but allows the maxi-band to stand for some time.
The last time Brazil changed its upper and lower limits for the real's maxi-band was at the beginning of 1996.
Finance Minister Pedro Malan said last week the government had no intention of changing its foreign exchange rate policy but would continue "perfecting" its twin-band foreign currency system.
His comment, which he denied meant changes were being considered, rattled the markets briefly.
Folha said there was no intention to speed up the rate of depreciation of the real currency. The newspaper gave no source for its report.
Government officials were not available for comment on the report.
